Modest uplift across methods

The ACCU market moved modestly higher during the week ending 12 June, with Generic ACCUs gaining A$0.15 from the Monday open of A$37.60 to close Friday at A$37.75. Premium methods maintained their spreads relative to generic pricing, with Plantation Forestry ACCUs holding at A$39.45 and Environmental Plantings remaining anchored at A$51.15.

Trade volumes remained subdued at 510k tCO₂e for the week, with the bulk of activity concentrated in generic and no-AD segments. The market structure remains characterized by stable premium differentials, reflecting consistent buyer preferences for co-benefit and environmental attributes.

Week's Key Driver

Modest price recovery in generic ACCUs supported premium methods. Safeguard compliance remained steady. Environmental Plantings pricing held firm after the prior week's repricing.

Market Condition

Stable and rangebound. Generic ACCUs trading A$37.60–A$37.95 with consistent co-benefit premiums. Low volumes suggest cautious buyer sentiment ahead of mid-year reporting.

Trade Activity & Liquidity

Weekly trade volumes totalled 510k tCO₂e for the period 8–12 June, representing a decline from the prior week. The majority of activity occurred in the generic (no-AD) segment at 380k tCO₂e, followed by generic at 100k tCO₂e. SMC trading accounted for 30k tCO₂e. The concentration in generic-equivalent segments reflects ongoing Safeguard compliance positioning and portfolio rebalancing ahead of mid-year reporting deadlines.

Low overall volumes suggest market participants are adopting a wait-and-see stance, with activity focused on essential compliance and portfolio management rather than speculative positioning. Premium methods saw minimal dedicated trading, with most flow occurring as part of broader generic/hedging activity.

Market Context & Outlook

Safeguard & Compliance

The modest uplift in generic ACCU pricing this week reflects ongoing Safeguard baseline compliance positioning. Entities reporting at mid-year are undertaking portfolio optimization to align surplus/deficit positions ahead of 30 June reporting. The concentration of trading in generic (no-AD) segments confirms this is compliance-driven rather than speculative activity.

Source: RepuTex ACCUsmart assessments; Jarden trade log

Method Development Pipeline

The persistent premium for co-benefit methods (Plantation Forestry +4.5%, SFM + ICB +27.5%, Environmental Plantings +35.6%) underscores sustained buyer demand for abatement paired with biodiversity, habitat, or ecosystem health outcomes. This structural premium is expected to persist as Australian organizations increasingly incorporate nature-positive criteria into procurement mandates.

Source: DCCEEW method approval tracker; buyer procurement feedback

Market Outlook

Short Term (2–4 weeks)

Generic ACCUs likely to remain rangebound A$37.50–A$38.00 as mid-year compliance deadlines drive steady demand. Premium methods expected to hold current spreads.

Medium Term (1–3 months)

Post 30 June reporting, look for renewed portfolio rebalancing. Potential volatility around method announcement timing (IFLM update expected mid-2026).

Premium Methods

Environmental Plantings repricing appears stable. SFM + ICB premium well-supported by demand. Forest methods likely to remain stable.
